about.intro_content: Prof. Zhu-Ming Guo is a Professor in the Department of Head and Neck Surgery at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou, where he has practised since graduating in 1983.
about.detailed_content: Prof. Guo has published more than 50 research papers on head and neck tumours, including submandibular salivary gland transfer to prevent radiation-induced xerostomia in nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients, laryngeal framework reconstruction using titanium mesh after partial laryngectomy, and management of complications from tracheal sleeve resection for thyroid carcinoma with tracheal invasion. His work spans functional preservation and reconstructive techniques across a range of head and neck cancers.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Zhu-Ming Guo

items.question: Does Prof. Zhu-Ming Guo accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to head and neck cancer at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Guo's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Guo specialises in head and neck tumour surgery, with particular expertise in functional preservation techniques and reconstructive surgery after cancer resection.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Does Prof. Guo help prevent dry mouth after nasopharyngeal carcinoma radiotherapy?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Guo has published 5-year outcomes on submandibular salivary gland transfer, a surgical technique designed to reduce the risk of radiation-induced xerostomia in nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients.

items.question: Does Prof. Guo treat thyroid cancer that has invaded the trachea?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Guo has published research on managing complications of tracheal sleeve resection for papillary thyroid carcinoma with tracheal invasion, a complex surgical scenario.
